sourceChecks.sourceText: and their sisters were Zeruiah and Abigail. The sons of Zeruiah: Abishai, Joab, and Asahel, three.
sourceChecks.previousContext: Ozem the sixth, and David the seventh;
sourceChecks.nextContext: Abigail bore Amasa; and the father of Amasa was Jether the Ishmaelite.

sourceChecks.sourceText: David had said, “Whoever strikes the Jebusites first shall be chief and captain.” Joab the son of Zeruiah went up first, and was made chief.
sourceChecks.previousContext: The inhabitants of Jebus said to David, “You will not come in here!” Nevertheless David took the stronghold of Zion. The same is David’s city.
sourceChecks.nextContext: David lived in the stronghold; therefore they called it David’s city.

sourceChecks.sourceText: He built the city all around, from Millo even around; and Joab repaired the rest of the city.
sourceChecks.previousContext: David lived in the stronghold; therefore they called it David’s city.
sourceChecks.nextContext: David grew greater and greater, for the LORD of Armies was with him.

sourceChecks.sourceText: Abishai, the brother of Joab, was chief of the three; for he lifted up his spear against three hundred and killed them, and had a name among the three.
sourceChecks.previousContext: and said, “My God forbid me, that I should do this! Shall I drink the blood of these men who have put their lives in jeopardy?” For they risked their lives to bring it. Therefore he would not drink it. The three mighty men did these things.
sourceChecks.nextContext: Of the three, he was more honorable than the two, and was made their captain; however he wasn’t included in the three.

sourceChecks.sourceText: The mighty men of the armies also include Asahel the brother of Joab, Elhanan the son of Dodo of Bethlehem,
sourceChecks.previousContext: Behold, he was more honorable than the thirty, but he didn’t attain to the three; and David set him over his guard.
sourceChecks.nextContext: Shammoth the Harorite, Helez the Pelonite,

sourceChecks.sourceText: Zelek the Ammonite, Naharai the Berothite (the armor bearer of Joab the son of Zeruiah),
sourceChecks.previousContext: Joel the brother of Nathan, Mibhar the son of Hagri,
sourceChecks.nextContext: Ira the Ithrite, Gareb the Ithrite,

sourceChecks.sourceText: Joab the son of Zeruiah was over the army; Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud was recorder;
sourceChecks.previousContext: David reigned over all Israel; and he executed justice and righteousness for all his people.
sourceChecks.nextContext: Zadok the son of Ahitub and Abimelech the son of Abiathar were priests; Shavsha was scribe;

sourceChecks.sourceText: When David heard of it, he sent Joab with all the army of the mighty men.
sourceChecks.previousContext: So they hired for themselves thirty-two thousand chariots, and the king of Maacah with his people, who came and encamped near Medeba. The children of Ammon gathered themselves together from their cities, and came to battle.
sourceChecks.nextContext: The children of Ammon came out, and put the battle in array at the gate of the city; and the kings who had come were by themselves in the field.

sourceChecks.sourceText: Now when Joab saw that the battle was set against him before and behind, he chose some of all the choice men of Israel, and put them in array against the Syrians.
sourceChecks.previousContext: The children of Ammon came out, and put the battle in array at the gate of the city; and the kings who had come were by themselves in the field.
sourceChecks.nextContext: The rest of the people he committed into the hand of Abishai his brother; and they put themselves in array against the children of Ammon.

sourceChecks.sourceText: So Joab and the people who were with him came near to the front of the Syrians to the battle; and they fled before him.
sourceChecks.previousContext: Be courageous, and let’s be strong for our people and for the cities of our God. May the LORD do that which seems good to him.”
sourceChecks.nextContext: When the children of Ammon saw that the Syrians had fled, they likewise fled before Abishai his brother, and entered into the city. Then Joab came to Jerusalem.

sourceChecks.sourceText: When the children of Ammon saw that the Syrians had fled, they likewise fled before Abishai his brother, and entered into the city. Then Joab came to Jerusalem.
sourceChecks.previousContext: So Joab and the people who were with him came near to the front of the Syrians to the battle; and they fled before him.
sourceChecks.nextContext: When the Syrians saw that they were defeated by Israel, they sent messengers and called out the Syrians who were beyond the River, with Shophach the captain of the army of Hadadezer leading them.

sourceChecks.sourceText: At the time of the return of the year, at the time when kings go out, Joab led out the army and wasted the country of the children of Ammon, and came and besieged Rabbah. But David stayed at Jerusalem. Joab struck Rabbah, and overthrew it.
sourceChecks.nextContext: David took the crown of their king from off his head, and found it to weigh a talent of gold, and there were precious stones in it. It was set on David’s head, and he brought very much plunder out of the city.

sourceChecks.sourceText: David said to Joab and to the princes of the people, “Go, count Israel from Beersheba even to Dan; and bring me word, that I may know how many there are.”
sourceChecks.previousContext: Satan stood up against Israel, and moved David to take a census of Israel.
sourceChecks.nextContext: Joab said, “May the LORD make his people a hundred times as many as they are. But, my lord the king, aren’t they all my lord’s servants? Why does my lord require this thing? Why will he be a cause of guilt to Israel?”

sourceChecks.sourceText: Joab said, “May the LORD make his people a hundred times as many as they are. But, my lord the king, aren’t they all my lord’s servants? Why does my lord require this thing? Why will he be a cause of guilt to Israel?”
sourceChecks.previousContext: David said to Joab and to the princes of the people, “Go, count Israel from Beersheba even to Dan; and bring me word, that I may know how many there are.”
sourceChecks.nextContext: Nevertheless the king’s word prevailed against Joab. Therefore Joab departed and went throughout all Israel, then came to Jerusalem.

sourceChecks.previousContext: Joab said, “May the LORD make his people a hundred times as many as they are. But, my lord the king, aren’t they all my lord’s servants? Why does my lord require this thing? Why will he be a cause of guilt to Israel?”
sourceChecks.nextContext: Joab gave the sum of the census of the people to David. All those of Israel were one million one hundred thousand men who drew a sword; and in Judah were four hundred seventy thousand men who drew a sword.

sourceChecks.sourceText: Joab gave the sum of the census of the people to David. All those of Israel were one million one hundred thousand men who drew a sword; and in Judah were four hundred seventy thousand men who drew a sword.
sourceChecks.previousContext: Nevertheless the king’s word prevailed against Joab. Therefore Joab departed and went throughout all Israel, then came to Jerusalem.
sourceChecks.nextContext: But he didn’t count Levi and Benjamin among them, for the king’s word was abominable to Joab.

sourceChecks.sourceText: But he didn’t count Levi and Benjamin among them, for the king’s word was abominable to Joab.
sourceChecks.previousContext: Joab gave the sum of the census of the people to David. All those of Israel were one million one hundred thousand men who drew a sword; and in Judah were four hundred seventy thousand men who drew a sword.
sourceChecks.nextContext: God was displeased with this thing; therefore he struck Israel.

sourceChecks.sourceText: All that Samuel the seer, Saul the son of Kish, Abner the son of Ner, and Joab the son of Zeruiah had dedicated, whoever had dedicated anything, it was under the hand of Shelomoth and of his brothers.
sourceChecks.previousContext: They dedicated some of the plunder won in battles to repair the LORD’s house.
sourceChecks.nextContext: Of the Izharites, Chenaniah and his sons were appointed to the outward business over Israel, for officers and judges.

sourceChecks.sourceText: The fourth captain for the fourth month was Asahel the brother of Joab, and Zebadiah his son after him. In his division were twenty-four thousand.
sourceChecks.previousContext: This is that Benaiah who was the mighty man of the thirty and over the thirty. Of his division was Ammizabad his son.
sourceChecks.nextContext: The fifth captain for the fifth month was Shamhuth the Izrahite. In his division were twenty-four thousand.

sourceChecks.sourceText: Joab the son of Zeruiah began to take a census, but didn’t finish; and wrath came on Israel for this. The number wasn’t put into the account in the chronicles of King David.
sourceChecks.previousContext: But David didn’t take the number of them from twenty years old and under, because the LORD had said he would increase Israel like the stars of the sky.
sourceChecks.nextContext: Over the king’s treasures was Azmaveth the son of Adiel. Over the treasures in the fields, in the cities, in the villages, and in the towers was Jonathan the son of Uzziah;

sourceChecks.sourceText: After Ahithophel was Jehoiada the son of Benaiah, and Abiathar. Joab was the captain of the king’s army.
sourceChecks.previousContext: Ahithophel was the king’s counselor. Hushai the Archite was the king’s friend.
